en.heading: 5 May: celebrating and safeguarding African World Heritage
en.origin: UNESCO's 38th General Conference proclaimed 5 May African World Heritage Day in November 2015. The observance highlights both cultural sites and natural landscapes, and addresses the pressures they face from conflict, climate change, poaching and development. UNESCO notes Africa's limited representation on the World Heritage List and the disproportionate vulnerability of some of its properties. It encourages conservation through cooperation and participation by young people and local communities. The exact original reason for the choice of 5 May and the first annual event are not established by the sources consulted.
en.promoter: UNESCO's General Conference formally proclaimed the observance in 2015; the sources do not name one verified individual proposer.
en.purpose: Promote protection of African World Heritage and give its communities and future custodians greater visibility.
facts: UNESCO proclaimed the day at its thirty-eighth General Conference in 2015.
The annual observance is held on 5 May and concerns natural as well as cultural heritage.

L'UNESCO segnala la rappresentanza limitata dell'Africa nella Lista del patrimonio mondiale e la particolare vulnerabilità di diversi siti. Il lavoro di conservazione coinvolge comunità locali e giovani. Le fonti consultate non dimostrano perché sia stato scelto precisamente il 5 maggio né quale fosse il primo evento annuale.

en.heading: 25 June: the people who make global shipping possible
en.origin: The 2010 diplomatic conference in Manila on training and certification standards for seafarers adopted the resolution creating the Day of the Seafarer on 25 June. The International Maritime Organization subsequently endorsed the observance in Assembly resolution A.1033(27) in November 2011. Its official meeting report confirms that first celebrations had already taken place in 2011, so the Assembly's endorsement was not the initial act. The day draws attention to the contribution mariners make to trade and to the risks, isolation and extended absences that can accompany work at sea.
en.promoter: The original decision came from the 2010 Manila conference; the IMO Council and Assembly subsequently endorsed it.
en.purpose: Recognize seafarers' contribution and promote safer and fairer working and living conditions at sea.

en.heading: From 24 October: a week dedicated to reducing the dangers of weapons
en.origin: Disarmament Week originated in the Final Document of the United Nations General Assembly's first special session on disarmament in 1978, resolution S-10/2. It opens on 24 October, the anniversary of the founding of the United Nations, to connect arms control with the Organization's mission of peace and security. A later resolution, 50/72 B in 1995, encouraged governments and civil organizations to keep taking part. The week is therefore the result of successive institutional efforts, not the initiative of one proven individual. en.heading: The first Saturday of July: two histories behind Cooperative Day
en.origin: The UN General Assembly adopted resolution A/RES/47/90 on 16 December 1992, declaring the first Saturday in July 1995 International Day of Cooperatives. That first UN date marked the centenary of the International Cooperative Alliance, founded in 1895. A second resolution, A/RES/49/155 in 1994, invited countries and organizations to observe the day annually starting in 1995. This is not the same as the earlier celebration promoted by the cooperative movement itself since 1923. The two timelines distinguish the movement's initiative from later formal recognition by the UN.
en.promoter: The International Cooperative Alliance promoted the earlier tradition; the UN General Assembly adopted the 1992 and 1994 resolutions.
en.purpose: Highlight how member-led cooperative enterprises can support livelihoods, economic participation and local communities.
facts: Resolution A/RES/47/90 was adopted on 16 December 1992.

Questo percorso è diverso dalla tradizione promossa dal movimento cooperativo già dal 1923. Le due cronologie distinguono l'iniziativa precedente delle cooperative dal riconoscimento formale delle Nazioni Unite.

en.heading: 14 April: when the first Chagas diagnosis entered public memory
en.origin: In May 2019 the 72nd World Health Assembly adopted decision WHA72(20), creating World Chagas Disease Day on 14 April. WHO documents the first observance in 2020 and explains that the date marks Carlos Chagas's first diagnosis of the disease in a human being in 1909, a Brazilian girl named Berenice. Chagas disease can progress silently for years and disproportionately affects populations facing barriers to healthcare. The modern campaign aims at earlier diagnosis, accessible treatment and prevention, rather than confusing the 1909 discovery with the 2019 institutional decision.
en.promoter: The World Health Assembly approved the decision in 2019, following an earlier proposal for a day devoted to Chagas disease.
en.purpose: Make the neglected disease visible, encourage early diagnosis and support prevention and treatment for affected communities.
facts: The 72nd World Health Assembly adopted decision WHA72(20) in 2019.

La malattia può progredire senza sintomi evidenti per anni e colpisce anche comunità con scarso accesso all'assistenza. La campagna moderna punta su diagnosi precoce, cure disponibili e prevenzione, senza confondere la scoperta del 1909 con la decisione istituzionale del 2019.

en.heading: 3 March: from ear-care awareness to World Hearing Day
en.origin: WHO's official chronology traces the initiative to a 2007 conference in Beijing that adopted the Beijing Declaration and designated International Ear Care Day. The date 3 March was selected because the figures 3 and 3 were considered visually suggestive of two ears. The first campaign therefore predates the name World Hearing Day, which WHO began using in 2016. Earlier activities in 2012 were described as International Day for Ear and Hearing Care. The distinction between the 2007 origin and the later name avoids pretending that a newly named event has no earlier history.

en.purpose: Promote hearing protection, early detection of hearing loss and access to ear and hearing care worldwide.

Nel 2012 le iniziative erano ancora presentate come giornata per la cura dell'orecchio e dell'udito. Distinguere il 2007 dal cambio di nome evita di cancellare la storia precedente della ricorrenza.

en.heading: 20 April: Chinese characters and multilingual UN work
en.origin: The UN celebrates Chinese Language Day on 20 April as part of the language-days initiative established by its Department of Global Communications in 2010. An official UN event description associates the date with Guyu, or Grain Rain, a traditional solar term, and with Cangjie, who is credited in legend with creating written characters. A legend is not archaeological proof that one person invented Chinese writing. The event instead gives visibility to Chinese language and culture as one of the six official language traditions of the United Nations.
en.promoter: The UN Department of Global Communications created the six-language days initiative in 2010; Cangjie is the subject of a cultural legend rather than the modern organizer.
en.purpose: Celebrate multilingualism and promote learning, literature and access across the UN's six official languages.

Una leggenda non è una prova archeologica che una sola persona abbia creato la scrittura cinese. en.heading: 23 April: Shakespeare within a wider history of English
en.origin: English Language Day is one of the UN's six official language days, introduced through a Department of Global Communications initiative in 2010. Its date, 23 April, is traditionally associated with both the birth and death of William Shakespeare. The playwright's writing profoundly influenced English literature and expressions, although the English language existed long before him and is used in many different cultures. The UN observance connects literature with equitable communication, interpretation, translation and multilingual understanding. A first separately documented ceremony is not established by the source reviewed, so no inaugural year is invented.

en.heading: 20 March: a Francophone anniversary in the UN calendar
en.origin: French Language Day is celebrated at the United Nations on 20 March within the six-language programme initiated in 2010 by the Department of Global Communications. The date also corresponds to the wider Francophonie anniversary associated with intergovernmental cooperation among French-speaking countries begun on 20 March 1970. These are separate institutional histories: the earlier cooperation is not the founding vote for a UN language day. The event recognizes French used by diverse communities in Europe, Africa, the Americas and elsewhere, and the importance of translation and multilingual access across the UN system.

en.origin: In 2021 the UN General Assembly decided to commemorate Global Media and Information Literacy Week, observed from 24 to 31 October. it.heading: 26 luglio: proteggere le foreste dove terra e mare si incontrano
it.origin: Nel 2015 la Conferenza generale UNESCO ha proclamato il 26 luglio Giornata internazionale per la conservazione dell'ecosistema delle mangrovie. La decisione riconosce che organizzazioni della società civile celebravano già il 26 luglio come giorno in difesa di questi ambienti prima della designazione formale di un'agenzia ONU. Il movimento di tutela precedente e l'atto istituzionale successivo sono eventi distinti. Le mangrovie proteggono le coste da erosione e tempeste, offrono rifugio a pesci e fauna e conservano carbonio nei suoli umidi. La prima edizione annuale guidata dall'UNESCO non risulta accertata separatamente nei documenti esaminati.
it.promoter: La Conferenza generale UNESCO istituì formalmente la giornata nel 2015 riconoscendo anche iniziative civiche preesistenti.
it.purpose: Promuovere ricerca, conservazione e gestione sostenibile delle mangrovie per biodiversità e comunità costiere.
facts: La proclamazione UNESCO fu adottata nel 2015 per il 26 luglio.
Il documento originario menziona precedenti celebrazioni non organizzate dall'ONU.
Le mangrovie proteggono le coste e offrono habitat a numerose specie.

en.heading: 17 October: living cultural traditions and their communities
en.origin: At its 42nd General Conference in November 2023, UNESCO proclaimed 17 October the International Day of the Intangible Cultural Heritage. This day concerns practices transmitted by communities, such as storytelling, performing arts, rituals, craft knowledge and traditions, rather than only monuments or museum objects. UNESCO describes its 2026 observance as the third edition, so the first annual edition followed in 2024, distinct from the founding vote in 2023. The date also recalls the adoption of the 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage. The community members who keep traditions alive remain central to their protection.
en.promoter: The UNESCO General Conference made the 2023 proclamation; States Parties and community heritage bearers organize activities.
en.purpose: Protect living traditions and foster respectful transmission, participation and cultural diversity.
facts: UNESCO proclaimed the international day in November 2023.
UNESCO's third annual edition was in 2026, following the 2024 debut.
The focus is on living community practices and knowledge rather than monuments alone.

it.heading: 17 ottobre: tradizioni culturali vive e comunità che le custodiscono
it.origin: Nel novembre 2023 la 42ª Conferenza generale dell'UNESCO ha proclamato il 17 ottobre Giornata internazionale del patrimonio culturale immateriale. La ricorrenza riguarda pratiche trasmesse dalle comunità, tra cui racconti, arti performative, riti, saperi artigianali e tradizioni, non soltanto monumenti o oggetti da museo. L'UNESCO presenta l'osservanza del 2026 come terza edizione: la prima si colloca dunque nel 2024, dopo il voto istitutivo del 2023. La data richiama anche l'adozione della Convenzione del 2003 per la salvaguardia del patrimonio immateriale. Chi mantiene vive le tradizioni deve restare protagonista della loro tutela.
it.promoter: La Conferenza generale UNESCO proclamò la giornata nel 2023; Stati e comunità custodi partecipano alle iniziative.
it.purpose: Proteggere le tradizioni viventi e favorire trasmissione rispettosa, partecipazione e diversità culturale.
facts: La proclamazione UNESCO risale al novembre 2023.
La terza edizione nel 2026 colloca la prima nel 2024.
Il patrimonio immateriale riguarda pratiche e conoscenze delle comunità.
